methodology: The study used a total of sixteen concrete mixes, with control, SSP (steelslag powder), SSP+RCA (processed recycled concrete aggregates) and RCA (recycled concrete aggregates) reinforced with various fiber dosages by volume.
research_objective: To develop and evaluate sustainable low-carbon fiber-reinforced concrete (FRC) made of steel slag powder, processed recycled concrete aggregates, and waste steel rivet fibers derived from industrial waste.

key_findings.finding: 1.4% WSRF mix had the best performance in terms of compressive strength and tensile strength
Optimal fiber content was found to be 0.8%
Recycled and waste materials, such as steel slag and recycled construction and demolition waste (RCA), can be used to improve the durability and engineering performance of concrete.
Steel fibers from industrial by-products like rivets can offer similar mechanical reinforcement with a reduced environmental impact compared to traditional virgin fibers.
Development of a sustainable low-carbon FRC with processed RCA, WSRF, and SSP.
Combining three different waste components into a single optimized concrete mix represents a feasible and innovative solution for sustainable construction.
Natural coarse aggregate (NCA) and recycled coarse aggregate (RCA) were used to replace natural fine aggregate in concrete at a 40% ratio.
